Let me think about actual bugs. The kernel loads pairs x[2k], x[2k+1] as z[k] = x[2k] + i*x[2k+1]. Complex FFT size M over z gives Z[k] where z[j] = x[2j] + i*x[2j+1]. Standard split: X[k] for real FFT of length N=2M:

Z[k] = sum_j (x[2j]+i x[2j+1]) e^{-2πijk/M}.

Standard formula: X[k] = Re{ Z[k] } ... let me recall the standard packing with z[j] = x[2j] + i x[2j+1]:

X[k] = 0.5*Re{ (Z[k] + conj(Z[M-k])) - i e^{-2πik/M}... let me derive.

Z[k] = E[k] + i O[k] where E[k] = sum x[2j]e^{-2πijk/M} (even DFT, size M) and O[k] = sum x[2j+1]e^{-2πijk/M}.

X[k] (size N=2M, real): X[k] = E[k] + e^{-2πik/N}·... actually X[k] = E[k] + e^{-2πi k/(2M)} O[k]? For DFT of size 2M: split even/odd terms: X[k] = sum_j x[2j] e^{-2πi(2j)k/(2M)} + sum_j x[2j+1] e^{-2πi(2j+1)k/(2M)} = E[k] + e^{-πik/M} O[k]. Yes, with E, O size-M DFTs, and e^{-πik/M} = e^{-2πik/N}.

Now Z[k] = E[k] + i O[k], Z[M-k] = E[M-k] + i O[M-k] = conj(E[k]) + i conj(O[k]) = conj(E[k] - i O[k]).

So Z[k] + conj(Z[M-k]) = E[k]+iO[k] + E[k] - iO[k] = 2E[k]. Wait conj(Z[M-k]) = E[k] - i O[k]. So Z[k] + conj(Z[M-k]) = 2E[k]. 

Z[k] - conj(Z[M-k]) = 2i O[k] → O[k] = -i/2 (Z[k] - conj(Z[M-k])).

X[k] = E[k] + e^{-2πik/N} O[k] = 0.5(Z[k]+conj(Z[M-k])) + e^{-2πik/N}·(-i/2)(Z[k]-conj(Z[M-k])) = 0.5[(Z[k]+conj(Z[M-k])) + (-i) e^{-2πik/N}(Z[k]-conj(Z[M-k]))].

Matches kernel lines 74-80? Kernel: sr = ar+br, si = ai-bi, dr = ar-br, di = ai+bi. So kernel computes Z[address] + conj(Z[partner]) = (ar + br) + i(ai - bi). Good — s = Z + conj(partner); d = Z - conj(partner) = (ar-br) + i(ai+bi). Then xr = 0.5(sr + wr*di + wi*dr), xi = 0.5(si - wr*dr + wi*di).

With (wr, wi) = (cos, -sin) of e^{-2πik/N}, so w = cosθ - i sinθ. X = 0.5[s + (-i)w d]. (-i)w = -i(cosθ - i sinθ) = -i cosθ - sinθ = -(sinθ) - i cosθ. So (-i)w d = -(sinθ dr + cosθ di) + i(cosθ dr - sinθ di) — wait carefully: complex multiply (a+bi)(dr+idi) with real part a·dr - b·di. a = -sinθ, b = -cosθ. Real: -sinθ·dr + cosθ·di. Imag: a·di + b·dr = -sinθ·di - cosθ·dr.

So X real = 0.5(sr - sinθ dr + cosθ di); kernel xr = 0.5(sr + wr*di + wi*dr) = 0.5(sr + cosθ·di - sinθ·dr). ✓. Imag: 0.5(si - sinθ·di - cosθ·dr); kernel xi = 0.5(si - wr*dr + wi*di) = 0.5(si - cosθ·dr - sinθ·di). ✓. Twiddle matches.

But: does Z's partner correspond to the correct bin under bit reversal? address = bitrev(k). DIF output is in bit-reversed order, so Z[j] (natural order) is stored at real[bitrev(j)]. Gathering at address gives Z[k]. partner = (-address)&(M-1) = bitrev((-k)&(M-1)) = bitrev(M-k). Gathering there gives Z[M-k]. ✓.

But wait: address = bitrev(k) — gathering real[bitrev(k)] gives the value stored at position bitrev(k), which in bit-reversed output is Z[bitrev(bitrev(k))] = Z[k]. ✓.

DC bin k=0: address=0, partner=0, so s = 2Z[0], d = 0, X[0] = 0.5·2Re Z[0] = Re Z[0]. Wait Re Z[0] = sum x[2j] = sum of even samples only! Imag part = sum x[2j+1]. But X[0] of the length-N real DFT = sum of ALL samples. Hmm! The formula gives X[0] = Re Z[0] = E[0] = sum of even samples. That's wrong?!

Wait — the standard split at k=0: X[0] = E[0] + e^0 O[0] = sum even + sum odd = Re Z[0] + Im Z[0]. But the kernel's general formula with partner=0 gives s = Z[0] + conj(Z[0]) = 2Re Z[0], so X[0] = Re Z[0] only. That's wrong!

Hold on — check: with partner = 0, ar = Re Z[0], br = Re Z[0], so sr = 2ar, dr = 0, di = 2ai, xr = 0.5(2ar + wr·2ai) where w for k=0 is (cos0, -sin0) = (1, 0). So xr = 0.5(2ar + 2ai) = ar + ai = Re Z[0] + Im Z[0] = sum even + sum odd. ✓! And xi = 0.5(si - wr dr + wi di) = 0.5(0 - 0 + 0) = 0. ✓. Good, the twiddle at k=0 (wr=1) fixes DC. Nice — the general formula is correct at k=0 because wi=0 there. Actually xi = 0.5(si - wr·dr + wi·di) = 0.5(2ai... wait si = ai - bi = 0. Right, si=0. Fine.

Hmm but the describer said Nyquist = ar - ai where ar=Re Z[0], ai=Im Z[0]. Nyquist X[M] = sum_j x[j](-1)^j = sum even - sum odd = Re Z[0] - Im Z[0]. ✓. But note: lines 83-84 use ar, ai gathered at... ar was overwritten in loop 69-72, ar = gather(real, address) at k=0 → Z[0]. ✓. But the Nyquist store uses ar - ai... correct.

Wait — but there's a subtlety: is the twiddle phase for k correct? k*(256//N): for N=256, phase = k; table for 256-point: cos(2πk/256) via fold min(phase,128-phase). k up to M-1=127. OK. For N=64: phase = 4k, up to 4·31=124. folded = min(phase, 128-phase) ≤ 64 ✓, index ≤64. For DIF stages: phase = (k & (half-1))·(256//width). k < M ≤ 128, half ≤ 64, phase ≤ (half-1)·(256/width) where width = 2·half → phase ≤ (half-1)·128/half < 128 ✓.

Twiddle check _twiddle: phase in [0,128). cos(2πphase/256): fold to [0,64], sign negative for phase>64. For phase in (64,128): 2πphase/256 in (π/2, π), cos negative ✓. sin = table[|64-phase|]: for phase<64: sin(2πphase/256) = cos(2π(64-phase)/256) = table[64-phase] ✓. For phase>64: sin(2πphase/256) = sin(π - 2πphase/256)... 2πphase/256 in (π/2,π), sin = cos(2πphase/256 - π/2) = cos(π - 2πphase/256) = -cos(...)? Hmm: sin(x) = cos(x - π/2). x = 2πphase/256, x - π/2 = 2π(phase-64)/256. So sin = table[phase-64] = table[64-phase] since |64-phase| = phase-64. ✓. And returns -sin. So w = (cos, -sin) ✓ = e^{-iθ}.

But wait — DIF uses twiddle e^{-2πi·phase/256} where the phase should be e^{-2πi·j·(M/width)/M}... DIF stage: butterfly on pairs separated by half, twiddle index j = k & (half-1), multiply by e^{-2πij/width}. Phase·(2π/256) with phase = j·(256/width) gives 2πj/width ✓.

So the algorithm appears correct on paper. Real bugs would be in Triton semantics: `tl.gather` — is that even a Triton function? In Triton 3.4, tl.gather exists? Actually `tl.gather` was added around Triton 3.2/3.3 for gather along an axis of a tensor. There's a concern about whether `_twiddle` tl.where sign: `cosine = tl.where(phase <= 64, cosine, -cosine)` — but phase≤64 fold already: for phase≤64 folded=phase, so cos positive. For phase>64 folded=128-phase<64, negated ✓. Phase can be 0... phase=64 exactly: folded=64, table[64]=0, sign positive (0 anyway).

Another suspicious spot: `left = k & ~half` — in Triton, `~half` on an int... ~ on constexpr int in Triton? half is a Python int constexpr; `~half` = -(half+1) in Python two's complement semantics — k & ~half where k is a tensor of int32. In Triton, `~half` computes bitwise not of the Python int = negative number; but k is int32, so & with negative python int... Triton might promote? Bitwise AND with -65 in two's complement int32: k & 0xFFFFFFBF... half=64, ~64 = -65 = 0b...1110111111. k & ~half clears bit 6 ✓ if treated as int32 two's complement. But Triton semantics of Python int constant: might be treated as int64 or int32. Likely fine.

Bigger risk: masking in the DIF loop for stage 0: width = M, half = M/2. left = k & ~(M/2), right = k | (M/2). lower = (k & half)==0. For k in lower half, gather left=k, right=k+half. Butterfly: lower gets a+b, upper gets (a-b)*w. ✓ DIF.

Also stage loop: `tl.gather(real, left, axis=0)` — real has shape [M]; left shape [M]. OK if tl.gather supported.

Potential issue: `tl.store(OUT + ... , 0.0, mask=k==0)` — storing float64 0.0 into fp32 tensor? Triton will cast. But `.to(tl.float32)` missing; Triton store may require matching dtype — it may auto-cast or may error at compile. That's a compile/runtime risk but observable.

The real potential bug candidates for claims:
1. tl.gather usage semantics in Triton 3.4 (does it exist, correct axis behavior) — a compile/runtime correctness risk.
2. `~half` bitwise-not with Python negative int constant semantics in Triton constexpr could mis-mask. In Triton, `~` on an int within a jit function is fine (int32/int64 semantics).
3. The `_twiddle` sign at phase exactly 128? phase < 128 always, fine.
4. Output Nyquist imaginary store of literal 0.0 dtype coercion.

Since I'm the Skeptic and can't run probes, I record claims. Highest-risk testable claims:

Claim A: The kernel produces incorrect frequency bins for some k due to tl.gather semantics or index math; specifically per-bin comparison against torch.fft.rfft in FP64 for each N in {64,128,256} will reveal mismatch. That's the generic correctness claim — the risk_map already identifies. Should be one strong claim with per-bin metric.

Claim B: literal `0.0` store into fp32 OUT in Triton 3.4 may fail to compile or cast incorrectly (nonfinite/garbage Nyquist imag). Testable: run Nyquist imaginary is exactly 0.

Claim C: `~half` negative-constant masking — actually likely fine.

Maybe better: a sharper mathematical check. Let me verify the Nyquist store more carefully. Line 83: OUT + (row*(M+1) + M + 0*k)*2 with mask k==0. That writes to element [row, M, 0]. Correct index. But note lines 81-82 already stored k values only for k < M; index k ranges 0..M-1, so Nyquist slot [row,M] written only by masked store ✓.

But wait — overlap: line 81 stores at (row*(M+1)+k)*2 for k in 0..M-1; fine.

One more check: imag of Nyquist should be 0 exactly — contract says imaginary part of X[M] for real input is 0 mathematically; storing 0.0 ✓.

DC: computed above = ar+ai ✓.

Hmm — but wait, DC: xr = 0.5(sr + wr·di + wi·dr) with wr=1, wi=0: 0.5(2ar + 2ai) = ar+ai ✓. xi = 0.5(si - wr·dr + wi·di) = 0.5(0 - 1·0 + 0) = 0 ✓.

So the math checks out; the claims should be about runtime behavior: per-bin agreement for each N, extreme magnitudes (FP32 output rounding vs tolerance: DC ~1.7e7, tolerance ~17, fp32 ulp at 1.7e7 is 2 → fine), subnormals fine.

Actually one more potential precision issue: with N=256, B=256, M=128, tensor real of 128 fp64 elements per program — fine.

Potential real bug: `tl.arange(0, M)` requires M power of 2 — 32/64/128 ✓.

I'll record 3 claims:
1. Per-bin correctness vs FP64 reference across N ∈ {64,128,256} (in_scope) — testable bin-by-bin max error vs tolerance.
2. Nyquist bin store: the masked store with literal 0.0 and index math may mis-write or Triton dtype coercion of 0.0 to fp32 may fail/produce wrong value — test last bin exactly equals reference within tolerance and imag == 0.
3. Extreme-magnitude FP16 inputs (all ±65504): accumulated FP64 error plus fp32 cast may exceed 1e-4+1e-6|exact| for mid-range bins where |exact| is small but intermediate sums are huge (catastrophic cancellation). This is a good adversarial claim: e.g. alternating ±65504 pattern where exact result is 0 but intermediate DIF butterflies have magnitude ~1e7; FP64 relative error 1e-16·1e7 = 1e-9 fine. FP32 output of ~0 fine. Actually FP64 internal precision is very good; the tolerance has absolute 1e-4 term. Probably passes. Still worth testing.

Maybe better third: tl.gather compile behavior per LOG_M specialization (open question). Testable: run all three N and each compiles and runs.

All in_scope per contract (all finite FP16 inputs, all N values). Record 3 claims.
